complaints.problem: Several correct answers are signposted by exact model vocabulary while distractors are extreme or anti-lesson, reducing no-tell quiz quality.
The laptop-lid cue is too device-specific and may feel arbitrary before the later sticky-note implementation plan clarifies the behavior.
This repeats the HopeLab parallel-first-pass lesson from example 1 with only a budget angle, so it adds limited new transfer range.
The forecast vignette is usable but thin: Yvonne, the launch, and the consequence remain generic, so it teaches the move without much before-to-after specificity.
The train-platform text exchange mostly restates the four villains and matching move without showing a concrete decision consequence.

parsedReview.oneParagraphVerdict: Ship. The chapter is clear, memorable, and unusually good about mechanism and limits: it explains why each villain distorts a different part of the decision and why WRAP improves odds without guaranteeing outcomes. The main weaknesses are craft-level, not blocking: quiz answers are often too easy to spot from signature phrasing, and a few transfer examples are thin or repetitive.
